rules.title: Optimise images
rules.what: Serve images compressed, in modern formats (WebP/AVIF where supported), sized to the display slot, with srcset for responsive variants and lazy loading below the fold.
rules.why: Images are most of the bytes of most pages. An image served at twice its display resolution costs double bandwidth and decoding for zero visible gain.
rules.how: Export at display size x2 maximum, compress (lossy quality ~70-85 where acceptable), provide srcset/sizes, loading="lazy" and explicit width/height to avoid layout shifts.

patterns.note: img without srcset; candidate if the image varies by viewport.
Raw jpg/png reference; modern formats with fallbacks are usually lighter.

verify.how: Audited images: format, weight and display slot recorded; weight within the page budget.

limits: PNG stays right for transparency, pixel art and technical screenshots; AVIF/WebP gains must be measured per image.

rules.title: Video sized to the need
rules.what: No autoplaying video (NR-SERVICE-005); serve video compressed, short, with a poster image and click-to-play; audio only when it carries information.
rules.why: Video is the heaviest content type by an order of magnitude, and background 'ambiance' videos play on every visit for near-zero task value.
rules.how: Host on a service that adapts bitrate, provide a poster, start on click, cap resolution to the display, trim intros.

patterns.note: Autoplay video; FAIL unless a user-gesture gate or muted decorative exception is documented.
Decorative background video pattern; verify it serves the page task.

verify.how: No autoplay attribute without documented justification; poster present; weight budget respected.

rules.title: Icons as SVG
rules.what: Use SVG icons (inline or sprite) rather than icon fonts or raster images; keep the sprite to the icons in use.
rules.why: An icon font ships a full font file plus a CSS framework for a handful of glyphs; raster icons scale badly and re-download per size. SVG ships exactly what is drawn.
rules.how: Inline critical SVGs, sprite the rest, remove unused glyphs at build time; keep SVGs minified and without editor metadata.

patterns.note: Icon font framework; count glyphs actually used before judging.

verify.how: Icon delivery method documented; used-glyph count matches the sprite content.

limits: An existing icon font used for many glyphs everywhere may be the lighter migration path; measure before rewriting.

rules.title: Limit downloaded fonts
rules.what: Limit web fonts to what carries the brand: few families, few weights, subset character sets, font-display: swap; prefer system fonts where acceptable.
rules.why: Each font file blocks or delays text rendering and transfers tens to hundreds of KB per weight. Most of those bytes are glyphs the page never displays.
rules.how: Default to system font stacks; for brand fonts, subset (latin, used glyphs), limit weights, self-host with preload for the critical one, fallback stack defined.

patterns.note: Google Fonts reference; verify subsetting, weights count, and self-hosting vs CDN choice.
font-face declaration; verify nearby subsetting (unicode-range) and font-display: swap.

verify.how: Font inventory: families, weights, subset ranges, loading strategy, fallbacks.

limits: Brand requirements are legitimate; the rule bounds their cost, not their existence.

rules.title: No unused or orphaned content
rules.what: Content published by a service is inventoried, dated and reviewed; orphaned documents, images and pages are removed or archived.
rules.why: Content accumulates forever: it is stored, backed up, indexed, and sometimes loaded, all for an audience of zero. Storage is a resource like any other.
rules.how: Inventory content with owner and review date (NR-SERVICE-007); check access logs before deleting; archive rather than keep online.

verify.how: Access-log review identifies zero-traffic content; retention decision recorded.

limits: Low-traffic does not mean useless (archival, legal); access data is one input, not the verdict.

rules.title: Open and lightweight document formats
rules.what: Deliver downloadable documents in open, lightweight formats (PDF/A for archives, HTML for anything web-displayable) rather than heavy office formats.
rules.why: A 4 MB docx that could be a web page makes every download pay for the format's convenience, and binds the content to one editor's roadmap.
rules.how: Publish as web page when it is for reading; PDF (compressed, structured) when it is for print/archive; office formats only when the user must edit.

patterns.note: Office document link; verify an editorial reason.

verify.how: Document download inventory with format, weight and audience reason.

limits: Administrative workflows often require office formats; the rule documents the reason rather than forbidding.

rules.title: Data minimisation at collection
rules.what: Collect, process, store and log only the data the service needs; define retention per data class at creation, not after the first incident.
rules.why: Data nobody uses still costs storage, backup, transfer, security and legal exposure. Collected data keeps billing forever after its purpose expired.
rules.how: For each data class: purpose, retention, deletion path. Prefer aggregation over raw, sampling over exhaustive, on-the-fly over stored.

patterns.note: Retention-smell identifiers; almost always a candidate.

verify.how: Data inventory with purpose and retention per class; deletion jobs exist and run.

limits: Legal retention obligations override deletion; they are recorded, not inferred.
